title: Rava bar Shmuel
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Berakhot 22b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.22b.11): Rav Papa, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua and Rava (Berabbi) bar Shmuel were eating bread together. Rav Papa said to them: “Give me [the honor] to bless.” … Rava (Berabbi) bar Shmuel said to him: “We have learned…” — “Rather, give it to me to bless, for forty se’ah fell upon me,” etc. Hyman infers from this that they were all colleagues; if so, it is clear that this is not the Rava bar Shmuel who lived in the time of Rav Chisda and Rav Sheshet.

Hyman suggests that possibly they deleted the word Berabbi needlessly, for the first was called Rabbah bar Shmuel, and this one came from the Land of Israel in Rava’s time and was called Rava Berabbi Shmuel. He suggests that possibly the first is the one mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.9.19) as Abba bar Shmuel.[^1]

notes.text: The Aramaic of Berakhot gives Rava berabbi bar Shmuel. The linked English gives Rava bar Shmuel. [Heilprin’s Rabbah bar Shmuel entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3148&lang=en) describes the meal and questions whether the earlier and later reports concern different men. The linked Yerushalmi has Rabbi Abba (bar) Shmuel, which Guggenheimer reads as Abba speaking in Shmuel’s name. Hyman suggests a distinction between the earlier and later figures and offers a possible identification for the earlier figure.
